newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bond yields up after whippy session.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bond yields up after whippy session.

text.p: *Australian bond yield closed higher after being whipped around in active trading with techical weakness in futures proving the overriding factor.
*Government report on enterprise bargaining due Thursday.
Australian bond yields closed higher after being whipped around in active trading with technical weakness in futures proving the overriding factor.

The December 10-year bond futures contract broke a three-month rising trendline just after the opening, and although Japan's quarterly Tankan report showed continued weakness, ensuring further flows from Japanese investors into Australia, the damage had already been done, traders said.
The local market also remains apprehensive ahead of the expected release of the Department of Industrial Relations' latest report on enterprise bargaining due Thursday.

"The enterprise bargaining appears to have taken on a greater significance since the Reserve Bank's quarterly bulletin, and is brewing up as the main figure of the week," said one trader at a European bank.

However, some analysts believe that the market has gone over the top on the issue, given that the RBA had also said in the same report that average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) is the most reliable guide for wages growth.
Meanwhile, Treasurer Peter Costello said that recent pay awards negotiated by the building industry of 21 to 24 percent over three years were not consistent with low inflation.

The domestic outlook is also under debate following this week's strong capital expenditure report, although it was the poor state of the Japanese economy which prevented the early sell-off turing into a rout.

The Japanese Tankan report was seen as putting any chance of a tightening in policy in Japan on the back burner for some time, maintaining Australia's yield advantage for yield hungry Japanese investors.
Meantime, U.S. Treasuries face a host of data during a shortened session later today ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving Day holiday.

The partial rebound saw the market pare some of its initial sharp yield spread widening against other dollar bloc bonds. However, the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread broke and held above 100 basis points, while the New Zealand market spread cemented its return to a discount to Australia.

The 10-year contract broke trendline support at 92.860 just after the opening but rebounded from last week's 92.805 low. However, the mid-92.900s again proved resistance in Tuesday's SYCOM session. -- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
